/-!
# Unit square: the rational distance problem

The unit square is the square in the Cartesian plane with corners
$(0, 0)$, $(1, 0)$, $(1, 1)$ and $(0, 1)$. It is not known whether any point in the
plane is at rational distance from all four of these vertices.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Unit square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_square#Rational_distance_problem)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- D19 in [Unsolved Problems in Number Theory](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-26677-0)
by *Richard K. Guy*

See also `FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.RationalDistanceProblem` for another formalization
of the same problem.
-/

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question (Guy D19 / rational distance problem): does there exist a point P ∈ ℝ² (anywhere in the plane, not necessarily inside the square) whose Euclidean distances to (0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1) are all rational; formalized as answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ P, ∀ corner, dist P corner ∈ ℚ (a distance of 0 counts as rational but yields no trivial witness since √2 is irrational); already present in the repo as RationalDistanceProblem.rational_distance_problem.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful proposition: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ P : ℝ² (= EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), Euclidean dist), ∀ vertex v ∈ {(0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1)}, dist P v is rational. Quantifier order/scope correct (answer(sorry) outermost, P over the whole plane, not restricted to the square), answer(True) = such a point exists, answer(False) = none exists; no vacuous/trivial witness (verified in scratch: dist (0,0) (1,1) = √2, vertices distinct, `∃ q : ℚ, x = q` ⇔ `¬ Irrational x`). c02 chosen because it is self-contained (imports only FormalConjecturesUtil, per AGENTS 'problem files normally import only ProblemImports'), introduces no bespoke definition (so no API tests needed, unlike c08), avoids importing another problem file (c01/c03/c07), uses the direct `∃ q : ℚ` rationality encoding rather than the double-negation `¬ Irrational` (c05), and has the best module docstring (cross-references the existing RationalDistanceProblem file, cites Guy D19 with the DOI the repo already uses). My edits: copyright year 2026 (current year), anchor link to the article's Rational_distance_problem section.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Unit square: the rational distance problem

The unit square is the square in the Cartesian plane with corners
$(0, 0)$, $(1, 0)$, $(1, 1)$ and $(0, 1)$. It is not known whether any point in the
plane is at rational distance from all four of these vertices.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Unit square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_square#Rational_distance_problem)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- D19 in [Unsolved Problems in Number Theory](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-26677-0)
by *Richard K. Guy*

See also `FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.RationalDistanceProblem` for another formalization
of the same problem.
-/

namespace InUnitSquare

open EuclideanGeometry

/--
Does there exist a point $P$ in the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ (not necessarily inside the square)
whose Euclidean distances to the four vertices $(0, 0)$, $(1, 0)$, $(1, 1)$, $(0, 1)$ of the
unit square are all rational?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 51]
theorem in_unit_square :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ P : ℝ², ∀ c ∈ ({!₂[0, 0], !₂[1, 0], !₂[1, 1], !₂[0, 1]} : Set ℝ²),
      ∃ q : ℚ, dist P c = q := by
  sorry

end InUnitSquare

items: The list-page entry is terse ('In Unit square:'); the precise statement is taken from the linked Wikipedia article section 'Rational distance problem': 'It is not known whether any point in the plane is a rational distance from all four vertices of the unit square.' (Guy D19).
The point P ranges over the whole plane ℝ² (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), not only over the closed square, following the article's 'any point in the plane'.

The unit square is fixed as the one with vertices (0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1), as in the article; the corners are written inline as a `Set ℝ²` literal instead of a bespoke definition (the existing `RationalDistanceProblem.UnitSquareCorners` lives in another problem file and was not imported to keep the file self-contained).

'Rational distance' is rendered as `∃ q : ℚ, dist P c = q` (equivalent to `¬ Irrational (dist P c)` used in the existing RationalDistanceProblem file). A distance of 0 counts as rational, but since the diagonal has length √2 this yields no trivial witness.
answer(True) corresponds to the existence of such a point; answer(False) to its non-existence.
The same problem is already formalized as `RationalDistanceProblem.rational_distance_problem` in the repo; the module docstring cross-references it.

reviewer_notes: The list-page entry is just the title 'In Unit square:'; the actual problem (per the linked article section and the decomposition table) is Guy D19, the rational distance problem for the unit square. All candidates agreed on this reading and none objected to the decomposition. The statement duplicates the existing `RationalDistanceProblem.rational_distance_problem` (mathematically identical; the two rationality encodings are definitionally equivalent) — the final file cross-references it in the module docstring; maintainers may prefer to merge rather than keep two files. The choice of the axis-aligned square with vertices (0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1) is WLOG by isometry and matches both the article and the existing repo file. Final file compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.
